about: Written by hand: the workspace reorganized by one dependency-injection rule (Sam, msg 1938), with Sam's decisions on it (msgs 1939, 1952, 1978, 1979, 1981, 1984, 1986, 1987), as a transformation of the current map. propose.py applies it to map-data.js and writes proposed-data.js; it stops if a trait has no decision, or anything named here is not in the map. A chart for planning, not a change to the code. Every entry has a status: decided (by Sam) or recommended (pending Sam). Item 7, the kkt-config breakup in config-split.json, is part of the proposal, accepted by Sam (msg 1979).
rule: Every trait a crate depends on is a contract, and it is declared by its consumers, not by the crate that implements it.

If a contract is used by more than two crates, it lives in its own contract-only crate (traits, pure value types, and test doubles behind `testing`). Its real implementations move to separate implementation crates that only programs depend on. Model: kkt-db (contract) and kkt-db-sqlite (implementation).
If it is used by two crates or fewer, each consumer declares its own contract, and the program adapts the implementation to it.
Used by: crates other than the definer and the implementers that take the trait in a public slot or call through it, in normal dependencies. Test-only use is listed separately.

new_crates.name: kkt-clock-system
new_crates.concern: The system clock and its sleep: `SystemClock`, a plain type that implements nothing; each program adapts it to kkt-clock's `Clock`. kkt-clock's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-entropy
new_crates.concern: The randomness contract `Entropy`, with `random_chars` as a provided method that takes the alphabet to draw from (msg 2011), and its test doubles behind `testing`.

new_crates.name: kkt-entropy-os
new_crates.concern: Randomness from the operating system: `OsEntropy`, a plain type that implements nothing; each program adapts it to kkt-entropy's `Entropy`. kkt-names' `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-container-os
new_crates.concern: The machine kkt-container runs Docker on: `OsHost`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-container's `Host`. kkt-container's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-service-os
new_crates.concern: The machine's service manager: `OsSystem`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-service's `System`. kkt-service's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-remote-access-os
new_crates.concern: The machine's `tailscale`: `OsHost`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-remote-access's `Host`. kkt-remote-access's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-client-config-os
new_crates.concern: The machine's files and the `claude` command: `OsHost`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-client-config's `Host`. kkt-client-config's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-diagnostics-os
new_crates.concern: Key file reads and network probes: `OsProber`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-diagnostics's `Prober`. kkt-diagnostics's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-lane-files-os
new_crates.concern: The disk and git under a lane folder: `OsDisk`, a plain type that implements nothing; the program adapts it to kkt-lane-files's `Disk`. kkt-lane-files's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-web-preview
new_crates.concern: The web page's preview over simulated data: `Preview` and `PreviewGate`, which implement kkt-web's `Source` and `Gate` themselves, as a program may (A7), with their settings; and the preview example, a dev-only program that serves the page. The preview's tests are here too. Its dev arrows to effect crates (kkt-clock-system, kkt-entropy-os) are the preview example's, which adapts them; the library depends on none.

new_crates.name: kkt-db-sqlite-db
new_crates.concern: kkt-db-sqlite's `SqlitePlace` and `MemoryPlace` adapted to kkt-db's `Backend`, `Connection` and `Evolve` (14 methods): `SqliteBackend`. The programs, kkt-rules' SQLite tests (kkt-store's before msg 2017) and the program's tests use it.

new_crates.name: kkt-server-listen
new_crates.concern: Binding the server to its socket and serving it: `listen` and `Listening`, which only the programs use. kkt-server's `real` feature moves here. It serves kkt-server's built `App`, so it needs axum (C7).

new_crates.name: kkt-backup-os
new_crates.concern: Writing and pruning backup folders on disk: `write` and `prune`, which the program calls. kkt-backup's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-shutdown-os
new_crates.concern: The operating system's stop signals: `StopSignals`, which the programs install and which stop kkt-shutdown's `Shutdown`. kkt-shutdown's `real` feature moves here.

new_crates.name: kkt-search
new_crates.concern: Search as text: the words of a text (FTS5 `unicode61`'s rule), a search's terms, whether a text matches them, and an excerpt around the matches, with `Word` and `Excerpt` (how an excerpt is drawn). Pure text: it knows no database. kkt-db-sqlite and kkt-db's in-memory backend use it; kkt-db's `Search` names its `Excerpt` (msg 2014).

kkt-clock::Clock.result: Shared contract: stays in kkt-clock, which becomes contract-only (Clock, Time, Span and the time text functions, FixedClock behind testing). SystemClock moves to kkt-clock-system as a plain type; each program adapts it to Clock (strict rule).

kkt-names::Entropy.result: Shared contract: a new contract crate kkt-entropy (Entropy, with random_chars(alphabet, len) as a provided method (msg 2011); the test doubles). OsEntropy moves to kkt-entropy-os as a plain type; each program adapts it to Entropy (strict rule). kkt-names keeps handles, IDs, name packs and the operator and admin names, and depends on kkt-entropy. kkt-rules keeps its token alphabet private; kkt-admission and kkt-names pass their own character sets.

kkt-identity::Identify.result: kkt-mcp declares Identify (with Identified and Identifying); kkt-server takes kkt-mcp's, gives that one value to /mcp, /mcp-admin and the web gate, and so makes one identity decision (A8). kkt-identity becomes kkt-identity-keymode, an implementation crate holding KeyMode, which implements nothing; kkt and kkt-keymode adapt it (3 forwarding methods; Q4). Before msg 2009 kkt-server declared a copy, and the adapter met both (6 methods).

kkt-store::Reads.result: Gone: kkt-store merges into kkt-rules, which uses kkt-db directly, so there is no store contract and no copies of the record types. Its one implementation had one consumer, and its queries hold decisions of the rules' own (msgs 2015 and 2017).

kkt-store::Writes.result: Gone: kkt-store merges into kkt-rules, which uses kkt-db directly, so there is no store contract and no copies of the record types. Its one implementation had one consumer, and its queries hold decisions of the rules' own (msgs 2015 and 2017).

kkt-db::Backend.result: kkt-db keeps the contract. kkt-db-sqlite implements none of it; SqlitePlace is adapted to Backend, Connection and Evolve once, in kkt-db-sqlite-db (14 methods). This changes the model pair kkt-db and kkt-db-sqlite. Its read and write become async, and the blocking pool moves to kkt-db-sqlite (msg 2012). All 14 methods forward: SqlitePlace exists only to meet kkt-db's contract (Q4). Database is gone: BackendExt provides the typed read and write over any Backend (msg 2014).

kkt-db::Connection.result: kkt-db keeps the contract. kkt-db-sqlite implements none of it; SqlitePlace is adapted to Backend, Connection and Evolve once, in kkt-db-sqlite-db (14 methods). This changes the model pair kkt-db and kkt-db-sqlite. All 14 methods forward: SqlitePlace exists only to meet kkt-db's contract (Q4).

kkt-db::Evolve.result: kkt-db keeps the contract. kkt-db-sqlite implements none of it; SqlitePlace is adapted to Backend, Connection and Evolve once, in kkt-db-sqlite-db (14 methods). This changes the model pair kkt-db and kkt-db-sqlite. All 14 methods forward: SqlitePlace exists only to meet kkt-db's contract (Q4). migrate and pending are Evolve's provided methods, so the adapter writes only version and apply (msg 2014).

decided_items.text: random_chars moves to kkt-entropy and takes the alphabet as an argument. ALPHABET becomes private to kkt-rules, for both making and spotting tokens. kkt-admission and kkt-names pass their own character sets. random_chars(alphabet, len) is a provided method of the Entropy trait, written in terms of below, so kkt-entropy is a plain contract crate (msg 2011).

Operator and admin names stay in kkt-names. AdminName is split: its name rules stay in kkt-names; bound_to and bound_in (tying the name to the key's hash) move to kkt-admission. kkt-store's private OPERATOR copy goes, and kkt-store takes it from kkt-names. (kkt-store merged into kkt-rules, msg 2017.)

The history from before kkt-db moves out of the program. kkt-store owned it (kkt-rules since msg 2017) as database-neutral facts (old 21 → core 1, 22 → core 2, the dropped handoff_note columns). kkt-db defines the neutral shape (today kkt-db-sqlite's Legacy). kkt-db-sqlite keeps only the SQLite part (user_version, the adoption). The program wires it and supplies the "upgrade with kkt 0.10 first" message.

kkt-store's testing offers an in-memory store on kkt-db's testing::MemoryPlace, and the fail-a-write hook; since msg 2017 they are kkt-rules' testing::memory and testing::fail_next_write. The tests of kkt-identity-keymode, kkt-mcp, kkt-server and the fake product dev-depend on kkt-rules for them, not on kkt-db or kkt-db-sqlite. kkt-rules' own tests run on both backends.

kkt-agent-client stops depending on kkt-watch. It offers plain methods with its own types (channels, handle, latest ID, message, wait, the admin polling included). The program holds a thin adapter implementing kkt-watch's Server and mapping the failures.
Both Failure enums stay; the program's adapter maps one to the other.

kkt-config is broken up by domain, as proposed (accepted in msg 1979): format and fixed facts move into the crate that owns them, tuning values become settings fields the program fills, operator settings and defaults go to kkt-settings or the program, and kkt-config keeps only what is truly cross-domain. The table lists every item.
Under each type, the page lists the contracts it implements with their methods, then its own methods, in both the current and the proposed map.

The strict rule covers only another crate's contract. A crate may implement its own traits: FixedClock implements Clock, the entropy test doubles implement Entropy, kkt-db's own implementations and MemoryPlace's Evolve stay, DryRun implements System, and SameSource stays in kkt-web and implements Sources (msg 1984).

kkt-server's Parts::new and Parts.db, its record_run, and the fake product's Product::start take kkt-rules' Db (since msg 2017; before, a store meeting kkt-rules' Reads and Writes). kkt-server no longer names a kkt-store type.
(Superseded by the adapter reshape, msg 2009.) Each program wired the Parts slots sources, gate and wording from its adapters; kkt-server now adapts all three itself (A6).
kkt-web's must-not: it depends on no rules, store, admission, identity or implementation crate; kkt-server and the preview implement its contract.
The preview example and the preview's tests move to kkt-web-preview, which has its own assembly. kkt-web's dev arrows to implementation crates go.

(Superseded by the adapter reshape, msg 2009.) Parts took a SourcesFactory and a GateFactory so the programs could adapt what kkt-server builds. With kkt-server adapting them itself (A6), neither is needed.

Shared adapters (msg 1984 item 8, accepted in msg 1987): an adapter that several programs and tests need lives once, in a composition crate, not in each program. kkt-db-sqlite-db adapts kkt-db-sqlite to kkt-db's traits (14 methods). kkt-store-rules is gone: kkt-store merges into kkt-rules (msg 2017).

kkt-format is dissolved (msg 1986). Formatter and what goes with it become kkt-mcp-formatter, in Surfaces, kind logic. NoticeWording moves to kkt-names and takes plain input; kkt-rules still declares OperatorWording, and kkt-server's Wording adapts it.

Layers say where in the system a crate sits, in both maps: Programs, Assembly, Surfaces, Access, Core, Data, Operations, Clients, Foundations and Dev-only. Each implementation crate sits beside its domain; the shared adapter crates sit in Data (msg 1986).

Each crate has a kind, written by hand: contract, logic, effect, composition, configuration or test support, and in the current map mixed. Boxes are outlined in their kind's colour. The generator checks what it can and reports mismatches; in the proposed map a mixed crate is a violation (msg 1981).

No crate in the proposed map is mixed, compositions included (msg 1992): kkt-server's listen and Listening go to kkt-server-listen, kkt-backup's write and prune to kkt-backup-os, and kkt-shutdown's StopSignals to kkt-shutdown-os. Only the programs use them. LogPolicy is configuration: it goes to kkt-settings, so kkt-provenance records it without depending on kkt-logs (msg 1995). Tagged "follows from Sam's rule"; C7 is decided: kkt-server-listen may use axum (msg 2010).

random_chars(alphabet, len) becomes a provided method of Entropy in kkt-entropy, written in terms of below (msg 2011). Its callers, kkt-names, kkt-rules, kkt-admission and kkt-web-preview, use it through Entropy.

Database's thread pool (spawn_blocking in Database::run) moves into kkt-db-sqlite. Backend's read and write become async, so kkt-db no longer needs tokio (msg 2012). Shown on Backend's and Database's docs and on both crates' third-party lists.

kkt-db is contract-only, with no logic crate beside it (msg 2014, replacing msg 2012's). Database disappears: its typed read and write become BackendExt's provided methods, over Backend's async read and write, with a blanket implementation that works through dyn Backend; its fault hook becomes testing::FaultyBackend, a backend that wraps another. migrate and pending become provided methods of Evolve, schema and schema_at Schema's latest and at, and the query checks Schema's check_ methods and operand_type; Step::apply_to stays. Search's text functions, Word and Excerpt move to a new crate, kkt-search (logic, A9, A10); Search and Hit stay in kkt-db.

kkt-store merges into kkt-rules (msg 2017): its queries, its decisions, the core's tables and their history, and item 4's testing helpers. kkt-rules uses kkt-db directly. Reads, Writes and the copied record types go; the record types only kkt-rules uses become private. Q1 is resolved. CLAUDE.md's rule on where database access lives changes with the code refactor, not in #409.

not_traits.note: Concrete types, not traits, so the rule does not apply as written. Shutdown is taken by kkt-server's build and kkt-mcp's transport; StopSignals, the real signals behind `real`, is used only by programs.

conflicts.title: Real implementations behind `real`, or in implementation crates
conflicts.text: PRINCIPLES rule 8 and CLAUDE.md put what touches the machine in the crate that owns the area, behind its `real` feature, and the rule moves it to implementation crates.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): each OS implementation moves to its own `*-os` crate as a plain type that implements nothing, and the consumer's `real` feature moves with it. The program writes one adapter per consumer trait: Host for kkt-container, kkt-remote-access and kkt-client-config, System, Prober and Disk.

conflicts.title: Reads and Writes: the store's contract, or the rules'
conflicts.text: Reads and Writes have one consumer, kkt-rules, so the rule has kkt-rules declare them. The plan has a second store (kkt-pro's) used through the same Reads and Writes, with the agreement test and the two-swarm test over those traits.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2017): kkt-store merges into kkt-rules. Its queries, its decisions (the swarm checks, lane version numbering, ChannelScope's translation), the core's tables and their history move into kkt-rules, which uses kkt-db directly as a consumer of a shared contract crate. Reads, Writes, the 36 copied record types, kkt-store and kkt-store-rules all go, with no adapter. Since msg 2015 showed that kkt-store decides things, A6 does not cover it. CLAUDE.md's rule that kkt-rules reaches the database only through Reads and Writes, and its kkt-store row, change with the code refactor, not in this chart.

conflicts.title: kkt-server's web adapters
conflicts.text: Step 6 made kkt-server's adapters to kkt-web's contract public, for a product that builds its own page; the rule would have the programs adapt them.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam). Reshaped after msg 2009 (recommended, A6): kkt-server is a composition, so RulesSource, RulesSources and AdmissionGate implement kkt-web's Source, Sources and Gate themselves, as today, and kkt-server mounts the page with them. The programs' 28-method forwarding adapters, the sources and gate slots, and SourcesFactory and GateFactory all go.

conflicts.title: Who adapts OperatorWording
conflicts.text: The rule says the program adapts; kkt-format's NoticeWording is wired into the rules by kkt-server, which is not a program.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): NoticeWording, in kkt-names, implements nothing. Reshaped after msg 2009 (recommended, A6): kkt-server's Wording adapts it once to OperatorWording and hands it to the rules; the wording slot and the programs' copies go.

conflicts.title: The model's own traits fall below the threshold
conflicts.text: Counted by the rule, kkt-db's Backend and Evolve have no consumer besides kkt-db itself, and Connection one, so they would not get a contract crate.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the strict rule (decided by Sam): kkt-db-sqlite stops implementing kkt-db's Backend, Connection and Evolve, and each program adapts SqlitePlace to them: a large adapter, 14 methods. This changes the model pair: kkt-db-sqlite no longer implements its contract crate's traits. The adapter lives once, in kkt-db-sqlite-db (item 15).

conflicts.title: axum outside the three crates CLAUDE.md allows
conflicts.text: CLAUDE.md: axum is the HTTP framework of kkt-web, kkt-mcp and kkt-server only, and its types do not leave those three. kkt-server-listen serves the App kkt-server builds, which holds an axum Router, so it needs axum and the Router.
conflicts.resolution: Decided by Sam (msg 2010): kkt-server-listen may use axum. CLAUDE.md will name it beside kkt-web, kkt-mcp and kkt-server with the code refactor, not in this chart.

withdrawn.text: Identify (one identity decision, or one per consumer) is not a conflict (Sam, via sage-cardinal, msg 1939): a shared trait does not guarantee one decision; the wiring does. kkt-server takes one identify value, which meets both consumer-declared traits, and gives that same value to /mcp, /mcp-admin and the web gate; the program wires KeyMode once. Since the adapter reshape (msg 2009), kkt-server takes kkt-mcp's Identify, so there is one trait (A8).

assumptions.text: SeededEntropy (repeatable randomness for the web preview and the fake product's differential test, never for tokens) counts as a test double, so it moves into kkt-entropy behind `testing`, not to an implementation crate.
kkt-service's DryRun wraps another System and only prints what it would do; it is the crate's own logic over its contract, not a real implementation, so it stays.
The program kkt counts as a consumer when its code names a trait (for example Box<dyn watch::Server>), as the definition says; kkt-watch::Server's one consumer is the program.

(Moot since msg 2017: with kkt-store merged into kkt-rules there are no copies.) "The record types Reads and Writes use" was taken as the 36 public types of kkt-store that the two traits' methods name (32), or that appear inside those types (AgentLaneRecord, ChannelNoteRecord, LaneSourceRecord) or inside StoreResult (StoreError).
(Moot since msg 2017.) kkt-rules no longer named kkt-store's Db: its Deps and CommandLine took a store meeting its Reads and Writes. Now Deps and CommandLine take kkt-rules' own Db.

An adapter that turns one crate's contract into another's, and decides nothing of either domain, is a composition. So kkt-server, which turns the rules' results into the page's views and adapts the wording, may implement kkt-web's and kkt-rules' contracts; without this, each program would need a forwarding adapter beside it (29 methods). Pending Sam. Withdrawn for kkt-store (msg 2017): kkt-review-373 showed it decides things (msg 2015), and Sam merged it into kkt-rules instead.

kkt-web-preview counts as a program, like kkt-fake-product: a dev-only package whose library exists for its own example and tests. So Preview and PreviewGate implement kkt-web's Source and Gate themselves, as FakeIdentify implements Identify.

An exception to the msg 1938 rule that each consumer of a trait declares its own: Identify has two consumers, kkt-mcp and kkt-server, and only kkt-mcp declares it. kkt-server's use (its web gate asks who the operator is, and it hands the same value to /mcp and /mcp-admin) is kkt-mcp's question, so kkt-server takes kkt-mcp's Identify. Two copies of one contract meant one adapter meeting both.

kkt-search sits in Foundations: it is pure text that the data crates build on and knows nothing of them, as kkt-clock and kkt-entropy sit under the crates that use them (msg 2014 left the layer to us).

Search (which stays in kkt-db) holds an Excerpt, the style of its excerpts, and Excerpt moves to kkt-search with the text functions (msg 2014). So kkt-db depends on kkt-search for that value type, and kkt-rules (kkt-store's code, since msg 2017), which states its excerpt style, uses kkt-search's Excerpt beside kkt-db's Search and Hit. The other choice keeps Excerpt in kkt-db as a plain value and has kkt-search's excerpt take its marks and window as arguments; then neither kkt-db's Search nor kkt-rules names kkt-search.

doc_edits.doc: The server over the admin endpoint, `/mcp-admin`, for `kkt watch --admin`: every channel, closed and hidden ones included, through plain methods; the program adapts it to kkt-watch's `Server` (item 5).

How notices name the operator, from the admin key's name or none: "The operator", or "The operator (via <name>)". It takes plain input, so kkt-names knows nothing of kkt-rules' Audit; the program's adapter maps Audit to it and meets kkt-rules' OperatorWording.
A database a store can run work on, through BackendExt. `read` and `write` are async: a backend that blocks, as SQLite does, runs the work on a thread pool of its own (msgs 2012 and 2014).

status_legend: "Decided by Sam" covers the rule itself (msg 1938) and what follows from it, and Sam's rulings: msgs 1939 and 1952, the strict rule (msg 1978), and item 7, the kkt-config breakup, accepted as proposed (msg 1979); msg 1984's fixes and its items 7 and 8 (accepted in msg 1987); and the layers, kinds and kkt-format's dissolving (msgs 1981 and 1986). "Recommended, pending Sam" is what rests on an assumption, which leaves the move that rests on A1 and the adapter reshape of msg 2009, which rests on A6, A7 and A8. "Follows from Sam's rule" marks what the rule requires once its checks run, without a ruling of its own (msg 1992): the effects split out of kkt-server, kkt-backup and kkt-shutdown.

strict.text: No implementation implements another crate's contract; the program always adapts (Sam, msg 1978). A composition may adapt too, being itself the adapter; where that rests on A6 or A7 it is pending Sam (msg 2009). A crate may implement its own traits: FixedClock implements Clock, the entropy test doubles implement Entropy, kkt-db's own implementations and MemoryPlace's Evolve stay, DryRun implements System, and SameSource implements Sources (msg 1984). Sam rejected the refinement of msg 1952, which let an implementation implement its one consumer's contract directly, because it leads to tight coupling.

renames.concern: Key mode's identity: `KeyMode`, a plain type that implements nothing; it decides who a caller is from the key that let it in and the avatar's token, and kkt and kkt-keymode each adapt it to kkt-mcp's `Identify` (A8).

The MCP tools' results turned into text or JSON, within the response size cap: `Formatter`, `Format`, its `Settings` and `MIN_RESPONSE_BYTES`. It is what was left of kkt-format, which is dissolved; `NoticeWording` moved to kkt-names (msg 1986).

kkt-clock.concern: Time: the `Clock` contract, kkt's time types `Time` and `Span`, the time text functions, and `FixedClock` behind `testing`. Contract-only: its real clock is in kkt-clock-system. The only crate that uses chrono.

kkt-names.concern: Avatars' handles, channel IDs, the name packs, and the operator and admin names with their rules. It draws randomness through kkt-entropy's `Entropy`, with its own character sets.

kkt-rules.concern: Every permission decision and every change, for agents and the operator, each in one swarm, and the core's data: the questions and changes the rules make, as kkt-db operations on a Db it is given, the core's tables as migrations with their history from before kkt-db, and the check that swarms stay apart. It uses kkt-db directly; kkt-store merged into it (msg 2017).
kkt-rules.must_not: Name a database or use a database library: it reaches the database through kkt-db's contract, which the program fills with the SQLite backend (msg 2017; CLAUDE.md's rule changes with the code refactor).

kkt-db-sqlite.concern: SQLite, the only crate that knows it: it opens a SQLite database, in a file or in memory, adopts a database from before kkt-db by SQLite's `user_version`, and copies one for backups. It implements none of kkt-db's traits; kkt-db-sqlite-db adapts it.

kkt-db.concern: The database contract, for any database: values, tables, keys and constraints; a narrow language of questions and changes (not SQL), with Schema's checks of which are valid; transactions, through Backend and the typed read and write BackendExt provides; search's Search and Hit; migrations as additions, run by Evolve's provided migrate and pending; the shape of a database from before kkt-db; and its own in-memory backend and fault-injecting backend behind `testing`. Every behaviour is a method of its own traits and types (msg 2014). kkt-db-sqlite meets it through an adapter.

kkt-server.concern: Assembling the server from its parts and running it: the rules, `/mcp`, `/mcp-admin` and the web page; recording each server run. Its parts take kkt-rules' `Db` and an identity meeting kkt-mcp's `Identify`. As a composition it adapts what it builds itself (A6): RulesSource, RulesSources and AdmissionGate implement kkt-web's contract, and Wording adapts kkt-names' NoticeWording to kkt-rules' OperatorWording. Binding the socket is in kkt-server-listen.

kkt-agent-client.concern: The shared MCP client for agent commands: avatar credentials, and reaching the server as an agent or admin through plain methods with its own types. It knows nothing of kkt-watch; the program adapts it.

kkt-mcp.concern: The agent and admin MCP tools, what the two share, their HTTP transport, and what agents are told about each tool. It declares the `Identify` it asks, which kkt-server takes too (A8).

kashkeshet.concern: The `kkt` command and everything it does on a machine: its subcommands and the files and environment they read, the settings and config file, the setup record, key files, how a client reaches the server, and one module per command that takes plain inputs. It holds the adapters the strict rule needs: one per contract it fills with another crate's implementation, except the database adapter it takes from kkt-db-sqlite-db.

kkt-keymode.concern: A second program that assembles key mode again from the shared crates with none of the `kkt` program's code, with its own adapters, as the strict rule has every program write, and the shared store and database adapters. The HTTP-only end-to-end tests run against it in CI. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-fake-product.concern: The shared crates assembled as a product other than kkt would assemble them, with two swarms and `FakeIdentify`, its own type meeting kkt-mcp's `Identify` (A8). It adapts the implementations it wires, as every program does, and takes the shared database adapter. Its tests check that nothing of one swarm reaches the other. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-admission.concern: Whether an HTTP caller is let in at all, and as which `Principal`: no key, which of the server's keys, or (for another program's `Identify` to judge) any bearer token. Also web sessions, the checks on the server's keys, and which admin name a key carries (`server_keys::bound_to`, `bound_in`).

kkt-container.concern: Running kkt in Docker: its Compose files, its folder, and the commands that set it up, start, back up, upgrade and stop it. It declares the `Host` it runs them through; the real one is in kkt-container-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-service.concern: Running kkt as a service under launchd or systemd, and the plan of what the service runs. It declares the `System` it works through, and keeps `DryRun`; the real one is in kkt-service-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-remote-access.concern: Sharing a service-mode server over the machine's existing Tailscale login. It declares the `Host` it works through; the real one is in kkt-remote-access-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-client-config.concern: MCP client configs and their file formats, so `kkt connect` can add kkt to a client. It declares the `Host` it works through; the real one is in kkt-client-config-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-diagnostics.concern: `kkt doctor`'s checks and their plan, and setup's wait for a new server. It declares the `Prober` it checks through; the real one is in kkt-diagnostics-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-lane-files.concern: Lanes as files: the `<lane>.md` format, reading and writing a folder of them, and the folder's git commit. It declares the `Disk` it works through; the real one is in kkt-lane-files-os, adapted by the program.

kkt-web.concern: The human's pages, through a contract of its own: `Gate` says who is viewing each request, `Sources` gives each viewer its `Source`, and every change is a checked form post. `SameSource`, its own `Sources` for a page with one view, and the page scenarios every source must pass (`testing`).
kkt-web.must_not: Depend on the rules, the store, admission or identity, or on an implementation crate: kkt-server and the preview implement kkt-web's contract.

kkt-events.concern: Notices of new messages, agents, channels and members, and of hidden agents and channels: one bus for the server, each notice heard only in its swarm, with a buffer per swarm kept only while it has a subscriber. The buffer's size is a setting the program fills (item 7).

kkt-watch.concern: `kkt watch`: waiting for an agent's new messages (or every channel's, as admin) and the line printed for each. The server, clock, saved place, output and its retry and wait timings are injected by the program (item 7).

kkt-backup.concern: Backup folders: their names, what goes in them and their file modes, and which to prune; the disk work is in kkt-backup-os.

kkt-shutdown.concern: The stop signal: `Shutdown`, whose clones share one signal. The operating system's signals are in kkt-shutdown-os.

rejected.text: An implementation may implement a consumer's contract directly when it exists to serve exactly one consumer (msg 1952). Sam rejected it (msg 1978) because it leads to tight coupling; the strict rule holds.

builds_removed.note: it no longer builds a kkt-db Database (C6)

shared_adapters.note: kkt-db-sqlite's store, adapted to kkt-db's contract (C6, item 8)
one forwarding method, written once in kkt-server instead of in each program (A6)

assembly.about: The programs' flows in the proposed map: the current flows with their items moved, except the steps replaced here, the wiring dropped here (named as in the current map) and the wiring added here (named as in the proposed map). propose.py stops if a step names an item, or a wiring a slot, that is not in the proposed map.

Database.text: A SqlitePlace for the database file goes into kkt-db-sqlite-db's SqliteBackend, a kkt-db Backend; kkt-rules' Db runs on it with the core's tables, adopting a database from before kkt-db as kkt-rules' history describes it in kkt-db's Legacy shape (msg 2017).

Run record.text: What produced this run is stored through kkt-rules' Db, and new rows carry its ID.

Parts.text: kkt-rules' Db, the program's adapters over the system clock, the operating system's randomness and key mode's identity go into the server's parts. kkt-server adapts the rest itself: the web page's sources and gate, and the notices' wording (A6).

wiring_add.note: SqliteBackend over the SqlitePlace is the kkt-db Backend the store runs on (item 8; msg 2014)

Database.text: As kkt serve's, through SqliteBackend. It adopts no database from before kkt-db.

Parts and config.text: The same parts as kkt serve, with KeyMode adapted to kkt-mcp's Identify; the admin key, if there is one, is the admin admission.

wiring_add.note: SqliteBackend over the SqlitePlace is the kkt-db Backend the store runs on (item 8; msg 2014)

Database.text: A database with the core's tables: kkt-rules' in-memory Db in its tests, a SqlitePlace file through SqliteBackend for its program. The product makes the second swarm in it.

Parts.text: The clock and entropy the caller gives (the system's, adapted, in its program; a fixed clock and seeded entropy in its differential test) and FakeIdentify, which maps made-up bearers to (swarm, role). kkt-server adapts the web page and the wording itself, as for kkt serve.

wiring_add.note: SqliteBackend over the SqlitePlace is the kkt-db Backend the store runs on (item 8; msg 2014)

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Flags give the address, the seed and the preview's settings; a non-loopback address needs an access key and names the hosts to answer to.

steps.title: Gate
steps.text: PreviewGate, with the access key or open, over the example's adapters to the system clock and the operating system's randomness; it implements kkt-web's Gate itself, as a program may (A7).

steps.title: World
steps.text: Preview simulates a swarm from SeededEntropy and the seed; it implements kkt-web's Source itself (A7), and kkt-web's SameSource gives every viewer that one source.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: kkt-web's router serves the page until a stop signal.

open_questions.text: Resolved (msg 2017): with kkt-store merged into kkt-rules, kkt-rules' unit tests use its own Db over kkt-db's in-memory backend, as src/tests.rs does today.

(on hold since msg 2009, now restated) The reshape leaves few repeated adapters: SystemClock (2 methods) and OsEntropy (1) in four programs, and KeyMode (3) in two. Repeating them is cheaper than a crate for each.

AdmissionGate forwards 5 of its 6 methods (sign_in_required, sign_in, sign_out, form_token, form_token_matches) to kkt-admission's web sessions: kkt-web's Gate copies kkt-admission's interface. If web sessions moved into kkt-web, as PreviewGate already keeps its own, the Gate would shrink to the two questions only the server can answer: does this key let a viewer in, and who is that viewer. That moves a security-relevant part between crates, so it is left to Sam. Recommended: move them.

66 forwarding methods remain whose provider exists only to meet one contract: KeyMode to Identify (3), SqlitePlace to kkt-db (14), SystemClock (2), OsEntropy (1), kkt-agent-client's Remote and AdminRemote to kkt-watch's Server (10), and the six -os crates (36). No contract reshape removes them under the strict rule: the provider cannot implement the contract, and the effects cannot sit beside their contracts without making those crates mixed. Recommended: accept them as the rule's cost. The six -os crates overlap (reading and writing files, running commands); one shared machine contract would cut their 36 methods to about 21, at the price of each consumer no longer declaring its own needs.
Resolved (msg 2017): Sam chose the merge. kkt-store merges into kkt-rules, which uses kkt-db directly.

RulesSource forwards 14 of its 21 methods: kkt-web's view types copy kkt-rules' records field by field. kkt-web may not depend on kkt-rules, so the adapter stays. kkt-review-373 notes two reshapes that would leave only copying: kkt-web takes its limits once, when the page is built, instead of asking the source; and Source's save_lane splits into create_lane and update_lane. The operator flag would then be the one translation left. Recommended: make both reshapes, so the page asks in its own terms; the copying stays as the cost of keeping kkt-web free of kkt-rules.

adapter_census.about: Every adapter in the proposal, measured against the code (msg 2009). Each method is forwarding (F): the same operation as a method of the provider, with at most a rename or a trivial conversion; or translating (T): it combines calls, reshapes records or holds logic. Copies: how many programs write it. Counted by hand from the code at the commit the map was generated from; the methods are each contract's.
adapter_census.before_note: As charted before msg 2009. Every provider kept its code in methods of the same name as the contract's, so every adapter method only forwarded; the column says where the translation stayed.
adapter_census.after_note: After the reshape. kkt-store merges into kkt-rules, so the store needs no adapter at all (msg 2017). kkt-server, a composition, holds the page's and the wording's translation itself, pending A6. The preview implements kkt-web's contract itself (A7), and kkt-server takes kkt-mcp's Identify (A8).

before.why: Each method calls kkt-store's Db method of the same name and copies the record across. The translation (73 kkt-db queries, such as channel_ids, which joins memberships with open channels, or append_lane_version, which reads the newest version before inserting) stayed in kkt-store.
Each method calls SqlitePlace's method of the same name. The SQL writing (save inserts or replaces and keeps the search index; search builds an FTS5 match) stayed in kkt-db-sqlite.
